context.architecture_overview: The architecture comprises two serverless Cloud Run microservices: a public-facing Storefront & API Gateway and an internal Factory Warehouse Fulfillment Worker. The Storefront serves the product catalog, interactive customizer, and cart, and exposes POST /api/v1/orders/checkout. Checkout validates mock payments against Secret Manager and publishes events to a Pub/Sub topic ('widget-orders-placed'). The Factory Fulfillment Worker receives push messages from Pub/Sub to atomically decrement inventory in Firestore ('inventory_ledger'), write invoice manifests to Cloud Storage ('invoices'), and transition order states in 'customer_orders'. Customer order tracking is queried via GET /track/{order_id}. To ensure topological validity, the Pub/Sub push subscription is provisioned after the fulfillment worker Cloud Run service is established.
context.summary: Full-stack serverless e-commerce platform for an industrial custom widget factory, featuring a FastAPI + Tailwind/Alpine.js storefront, dynamic configurator, Firestore ledger, Secret Manager payment validation, and an asynchronous factory fulfillment Cloud Run worker driven by Pub/Sub.

recorded_system:
### SERVICE TOPOLOGY (`service_topology`, always set)
Describe the workload's compute as typed data. The platform renders all compute and all service-to-service wiring from it; it never reads the specification text for this.
   - `services`: every compute service the specification asks the platform to deploy, each with `name` (lower-case letters, digits and '-', starts with a letter, at most 40 characters), `kind` and a one-line `purpose`. Add `scaling` only when the specification states instance counts. `[]` means no compute (foundation-only).
   - Kinds:
     * `cloudrun`: primary or secondary; any number; callee of http edges; can call others (has env vars); can launch gce-workers.
     * `event-worker`: primary or secondary; at most 1 per workload; callee of pubsub edges; cannot call others (no env vars).
     * `gke-autopilot`: primary only; at most 1 per workload; never an edge callee; cannot call others (no env vars).
     * `gce-bastion`: primary only; at most 1 per workload; never an edge callee; cannot call others (no env vars).
     * `gce-worker`: secondary only; any number; callee of launch edges; can call others (has env vars).
   - `primary_service`: the service deployed on module "compute"; its kind MUST equal `compute_archetype`; null only when `services` is []. `target_compute_services` lists the same names, primary first.
   - `edges`: one entry per caller -> callee call (`protocol` `http` to a cloudrun callee, `pubsub` to the event-worker). The caller receives `<BASE>_URL` and `<BASE>_AUDIENCE` (http) or `<BASE>_TOPIC` (pubsub); `<BASE>` is `env_key_base` or the callee name upper-cased with '-' as '_'. Edges MUST be acyclic: never A -> B and B -> A; route one direction through Pub/Sub or invert the call. GKE and gce-bastion workloads are reached through their own networking, never through an edge.
   - VM workers the app starts on demand (e.g. ephemeral Spot VMs running a batch script): one `gce-worker` service each (never the primary; add `vm` {machine_type, spot, disk_size_gb} only when the specification states the VM shape) and a `launch` edge from the cloudrun service that starts it; that caller receives `<BASE>_INSTANCE_TEMPLATE`, `<BASE>_ZONE` and `<BASE>_NAME_PREFIX`. A worker reads resources like a service but is never an edge caller; worker names must not be prefixes of each other.
   - `resources`: only these types: `google_storage_bucket` (name), `google_pubsub_topic` (name/id), `google_pubsub_subscription` (name), `google_secret_manager_secret` (secret_id/id), `google_redis_instance` (host/port), `google_sql_database_instance` (connection_name/private_ip_address), `google_firestore_database` (name), `google_bigquery_dataset` (dataset_id). Give each the Terraform `logical_name` the IaC will use and, per service that reads it, `consumers` with the exact environment variable name (`env_key`). Anything else is described in a service's `purpose`. Resources are never services.
   - Single-service default: one `cloudrun` service named after `product_id`, no edges.
